header.text: Each house of Congress has important leaders, many of whom are determined by which party is in the majority. Look at the chart explaining the functions of some of those leaders. Then answer the question below.

alternativeText.text: A chart showing some of the different roles in Congress and their main functions.   In the House of Representatives, the Speaker of the House is considered the head of the House. They select many committee members and decide which committee will review each bill.  The majority leader serves as the spokesperson for their party, schedules bills, and keeps their party's legislative agenda. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of representatives.  In the Senate, the vice president of the United States serves as the president of the Senate. They are responsible for breaking tie votes. The president pro tempore serves as the head of the Senate when the president of the Senate is absent. The majority leader serves as a spokesperson for the majority party, but also for the Senate as a whole. They schedule bills and keep the legislative agenda for their party. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of senators.

header.text: Each house of Congress has important leaders, many of whom are determined by which party is in the majority. Look at the chart explaining the functions of some of those leaders.

alternativeText.text: A chart showing some of the different roles in Congress and their main functions.   In the House of Representatives, the Speaker of the House is considered the head of the House. They select many committee members and decide which committee will review each bill.  The majority leader serves as the spokesperson for their party, schedules bills, and keeps their party's legislative agenda. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of representatives.  In the Senate, the vice president of the United States serves as the president of the Senate. They are responsible for breaking tie votes. The president pro tempore serves as the head of the Senate when the president of the Senate is absent. The majority leader serves as a spokesperson for the majority party, but also for the Senate as a whole. They schedule bills and keep the legislative agenda for their party. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of senators.

A case starts in the U.S. district courts, which hears all federal court cases and has 94 courts across the country. elements.text: The House of Representatives votes to impeach the president. Impeachment is similar to charging the president with a crime.

The federal government is the national government of the United States.  It has the power to make decisions that affect the entire country.
State
Within the United States, there are 50 different state governments. State governments have the power to make many decisions that affect only their state.
Local
Within each state, there are many cities, towns, and counties. Each one has a local government to meet the needs of the local community.

textContent.text: In the 1930s and 1940s, two researchers named Kenneth and Mamie Clark used dolls to conduct three studies about African American students' self-esteem. They found that, in schools that were segregated by race, African American students believed that dolls with white skin were "good" and dolls with brown skin were "bad."
The Clarks concluded that segregated schools made African American students feel less valuable than white students. Therefore, segregated schools harmed African American students' self-esteem.
